hints: Count apples and bananas by weight first.
For total weight w, sum appleCount[i]*bananaCount[w-i].
This is polynomial convolution, computable with FFT.
analogy: Multiplying two generating polynomials combines every apple weight with every banana weight.
example: Apples [1,2] and bananas [1,1] give counts 2 for sum 2 and 2 for sum 3.
algorithm: Form coefficient arrays A and B of frequencies by weight. Compute their convolution with a sufficiently precise FFT and round each resulting coefficient to the nearest integer, or use enough NTT moduli and reconstruct exact coefficients. Print coefficients 2 through 2k.
correctness: Coefficient w of the product is the sum over i of A[i]*B[w-i], exactly the number of ordered choices of one apple and one banana of total weight w.
complexity: For maximum weight k, O(k log k+n+m) time and O(k) space; exact NTT reconstruction requires a modulus product exceeding n*m.
